tiles: Right outcome once the investor confirms the pre-filled answers (simulated), current build, 3 of 3 runs
Reason read correctly by the AI (rules-only baseline: 79%)
Rules-only baseline outcome: the same as the AI on this test set
summary:
**What was tested.** On 6 Nov, on the current build: 28 fresh test messages (22 real public comments drawn at random and never used in development, plus 6 status texts) and 6 guardrail tests. Each was run 3 times and compared with hand labels.

**How the helper works.** The AI pre-fills what the message says. The investor confirms the app status, whether money was taken and the reason, in one tap. Fixed rules then pick the reason and the fix.

**Pre-fill accuracy before confirmation** (AI over 3 runs / rules-only baseline):

| Fact | AI | Rules only |
|---|---|---|
| App status | 50–61% | 71% |
| Money taken | 61–75% | 75% |
| Reason | 82–89% | 79% |
| Recent change | 96% | 96% |

**Honest result.** On this small test set, simple keyword rules read the facts about as well as the AI (90 of 112 facts vs 81–90) and need no more corrections. The AI was better at the reason in messy real comments: it was right where the rules were wrong on 5 messages, the reverse on 3. It was worse at the app status. Where the AI clearly adds something rules can't is turning speech in English, Hindi or Hinglish into text. Production plan: rules first for known wordings, which is faster and cheaper, and the AI for voice and for wording the rules can't place, validated on a new labelled set.

**Guardrails.** 6 of 6 handled, 0 violations. Two of the six mix a failed payment with a fund question. Since 5 Nov they get a visible "can't advise on funds" notice and help with the payment only. Under the original rule, which counted only a full refusal, the score is 4 of 6.

**Re-run history.** The 4 Nov runs (28/28 after confirmation) were on an earlier build. The 6 Nov re-run found that new help routing sent 3 failure messages to a help answer first (25/28). A message that describes a failure now goes to the fix flow (27/28). The remaining miss is a debit complaint that names no failure and asks for customer care; it gets the support answer with a "find out why" button.

**Release checks (every deploy).** 76 QA cases (76/76 with the AI, 76/76 rules-only), 27 end-to-end user scenarios, all 336 answer combinations, and 6 screen sizes in light and dark mode.

**Limits.** One labeller (three passes, settled against written rules); a small test set; a free AI tier, with a rules-only mode when it is busy.
